chapter: Brown's Band in Chicago and New York
title: Reisenweber's offer and leaving New York
summary: A $25-a-week offer was refused; Loyacano took a boat back to New Orleans.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Well, then, you stayed then at this, uh, restaurant in New York for how long?

Oh, I don't know. Approximately. Possibly four weeks. And that was it. In the meantime, I told Raymond, I said, we're, we're not going to make it here. These people not going for this stuff. So, we went down to Rising Webbers. It was up there. Sophie Tucker was on. It was a big place.

And, uh, Sophie Tucker was working upstairs. Mm-hmm. It was so big that it had a terrace around it. Mm-hmm. On the, uh, two-story. Mm-hmm. So, we saw Mr. Schultz. I'm pretty sure that was his name manager. Then we told him what we had. He said, all right. He said, I'll tell you what I'll do. He said, I'll give you boys a contract for two weeks and $25 a man a week. But after the money we're getting in Chicago, that was peanuts.
How much were you getting at, uh, what do you call it? The Century? Is that what you...
Century Theater. How much were you getting?

Well, we were getting $50, I think, a week. So, none of them were interested. We could have had all the gravy that the Dixieland Band got, because we were there before them, and we could have been hired before them. We could have worked the place. And, uh, I told them, well, we had a meeting. We talked it over, and I said, well, why don't we just go and take the job and wire Frisco? I said, we can pitch in, pitch in a couple of dollars a piece, and get Frisco up here to do that dance, that Frisco dance that he did. And his girlfriend, Loretta McDermott, had lived in New York, up in the Bronx, on the 53rd Street. And there'd been peaches for her right in the neighborhood. So, uh, the boys said, no, wasn't enough money. It wasn't this, it wasn't that. So, I said, all right, do what you please. And then we got out of the job. There wasn't anything else that was brewing around. Harry Fitzgerald turned out to be the kind of guy I thought he was. And so I got aboard a boat, United Fruit Company, liner, and came on down to New Orleans.
